challenge.better_approach: Considered the idea's own shape — a verb that journals a path's standing bytes against the journal's last sha_after, with no park. Since 0f8aefbba1d0 every loss the door can see is parked with the full entry (who, why, stack), so re-landing the parked entry keeps the original attribution; journaling standing bytes would re-attribute the write to whoever runs the repair. Considered re-landing automatically at the next door write — that is a hidden act inside an unrelated write, and it could run mid-rewrite under someone else's lock; a named verb is the plain thing.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That the original entry's sha_before still matching the journal's last sha_after for the path means nothing wrote the record in between; a write in between moves the journal's last sha_after, so the guard holds. That the park is only appended by _append (it lives under the git dir, not a record).
challenge.prior_art: Consulted the artifact charter (cairn/tools/artifact/intention+why.json) and the ticket corpus: 0f8aefbba1d0 parks and names the re-land as a later act (its bounds.out); 7bb99eed0629 attributes orphaned changes in the tree, not parked journal lines; hand-edit parks bytes for Akien's approval, a different lane (bytes written around the door, not a door write whose line was lost). genesis journals never-journaled records only. Nothing re-lands.
challenge.real_collision: None: the chain contract stands (_append chains the copy); the original entry id never stood in the journal, so relanded_from names it without duplicating a line.

answers.falsifier: Red: on the code at a73b82545 there is no reland; a parked entry stays parked and the record's staged bytes fail check_staged. Green: (1) a parked entry whose record still stands at its sha_after and whose sha_before is the journal's last for its path is appended once, chained, verify_chain clean, check_staged passes, and the park is empty; (2) a parked entry whose record moved on, or whose sha_before is not the journal's last, stays parked, is named, nothing is appended, and the verb exits 1; (3) re-running reland on an emptied park, or over an entry already landed, appends nothing.
answers.how: artifact.py gains reland(name, why): under door_lock, read orphan_park(root); for each parked entry in order: if the journal already holds it (an entry whose relanded_from or entry is its id) drop it from the park; else if the journal's last sha_after for its path equals its sha_before and the record's standing bytes hash to its sha_after, append a copy (prev/entry recomputed by _append, plus relanded_from, relanded_why, relanded_by) and drop it from the park; else keep it parked and name why. The park is rewritten with what stays (plus any line parked while reland ran). __main__.py adds the `reland` verb; exit 1 when anything stays parked. Red-first proof in cairn/tools/artifact/proofs/.
answers.traces_to: Law 7 — errors are permanent in records of truth: the journal is the record of who wrote every record, and a parked line the door cannot re-land leaves the commit blocked ('changed around the door') or invites a scratch script that writes around the door (measured 2026-11-13, f695fac922cd's repair). Law 1 — the repair is one command, not re-derived each time.
answers.what: A journal entry the artifact door parked because git replaced the journal under its append is re-landed through the door by one command, `cairn artifact reland <root> --why`, chained on the journal's tail, and only when the record still stands at the bytes the entry describes.

bullets.text: Scoped to parked entries at the orchestrator's ask (2026-11-13): since 0f8aefbba1d0 the door parks every line it sees lost, so the idea's 'journal standing bytes with no park' case has no live producer left except hand edits, which have their own lane.

title: A journal entry the artifact door parked because git replaced the journal under its append is re-landed through the door
